criteria.rationale: Examined the spec constraints, the A->B->A paragraph, the ADR budgets and the follow-up list. Verified facts: captured-byte identity, final audit, single retry and guarded writes exist in source (governance_read_view.go, governance_write_guard.go). Accepted risks are explicit: uncooperative external writers/ABA are outside the guarantee, no universal filesystem transaction is claimed, and F3 is owned until 2026-12-06. Unresolved limits are kept rather than hidden: tech-debt INCOMPLETE (two historical specs unreadable), the prior global structural check on b7b5680f is not relabelled current, and my own session could not execute commands. Conclusion: assumptions are separated correctly from verified facts.

The sealed check runs with -race over the pose, cli and mcpserver read-view, guard and index selections. In source, view reads serialize on v.mu, the audit waits for active readers (governance_read_view.go:2049-2053), operation budgets use budgetMu, and the write lease uses atomic plus once-release with canonical root ordering (governance_write_guard.go:78-187, 472-528).

ObligationReport stays schema v1 with an additive read_view object (schema v1); review and closeout add an optional read_view field (review_closeout.go:420-430); the MCP catalog golden documents read_view. CLI/MCP result parity is covered by the sealed check.

Guard refusals are typed sentinels wrapped in GovernanceWriteGuardError without host paths (governance_write_guard.go:23-65). Read-view failures use ErrGovernanceReadViewChanged/Unknown with clipped, bounded summaries (governance_read_view_capture.go:88-137), and index build failures map to stable codes. F3 is the remaining low-severity untyped classification.
Projection, review, closeout, index build and writers all consume the same view/guard primitives across the pose, cli and mcpserver packages; the sealed integration selection covers these boundaries.

Limitations name the producer and reason, changed paths are root-relative display paths, roots are exposed as digests, and error summaries are capped at 8 producers, 4 reasons and 2048 bytes (governance_read_view_capture.go:88-137).

Examined the report and Obligation schema versions (both remain 1), the additive read_view, the documented treatment of legacy reports without a binding as readable but non-authorizing (POSE.md:372), and the MCP catalog descriptions. Historical records are not rehashed. Conclusion: compatible, with the additions explicitly documented.

R1-F1 is fixed: the registry final audit reaches metadata, so review, closeout and projection report unknown and do not keep approval or terminal status on a change (governance_read_view.go:388-408; regressions in governance_read_view_d7_probe_test.go:225-375). Positive controls (stable, recovered once) remain current.
CLI and MCP surfaces consume the same domain projection and review evaluation; sealed parity checks pass.

Root cause per the spec: CurrentObligationSnapshot did not bind journal/subject bytes and the closure was not audited after the producers ran. D2 extends Files with per-operation capture that serves the same bytes to every producer; the final audit plus one retry addresses R3; D3 makes the disclosure additive; D4 guards writers per root with B14 CAS for R6/R7; D5-D7 bound budgets and per-scope views from measured corpora; D8 and D9 address instance policy and the executable-hash bound. The structure check passed.

mappings.rationale: The validation matrix adds the required race check governance-read-view-integration over the B34 test selection and explicit -count=1 build/test/vet checks, qualifying R10's fixtures and fault injection as Validation V7 requires.
The spec constraint requires the B34 ADR to be accepted before the contract changes; the ADR records the bounded operation-scoped view and its budgets on which decisions D2-D9 rest.

delegation.json is instance-only configuration of the independent-review agents and is excluded from the embedded scaffold (distpolicy.go:115-118), as D8 decides. Its narrowed session regex responds to the retained capture failure rrn-db41024e48aa50af. It contains no secrets.

criteria.rationale: POSE.md:372-373 (and its pt-BR and scaffold copies) describe snapshot.read_view, the ID binding, separate coherence/coverage/freshness, 'current' meaning only the final audit instant, legacy non-authorization and the budgets; the ADR documents 25,000 records, 512 MiB, 8 MiB and 16 roots; the MCP catalog descriptions mention read_view freshness and limitations. They match the runtime behaviour I read.

Captured bytes, entries, links and errors define the ID (metadataSingle); mtime and identity are included, so even same-size edits change it. Interleaving triggers one retry, then coherent=false/unknown with incomplete coverage, and the registry path no longer relabels a changed view as current (R1-F1 fixed). Coverage loss blocks Complete (obligation_projection.go:341-348). Effects revalidate under the per-root guard with B14/B15 CAS (start.go, action_request.go, index_generation.go). External-writer and A->B->A limits are explicit. There is no inter-operation cache.

Index failures say whether anything was written and tell the user to rerun `pose index` or `pose index --verify` (cli/index_generation_build.go:39-117); guard busy/unavailable errors name the operation and root label; read-view limitations name producer and reason. F3 does not hurt the user-visible message, only how it is classified.

R1-R10 are exercised by the sealed B34 race selection plus the obligation-projection, writer-publication, index-generation and state-attention checks; the R3/R5 registry interleaving gap from round 1 now has dedicated regressions.

Compared the change list with the spec's artifact plan: every changed source and governance file is declared, and the instance delegation policy is covered by D8. No watcher, daemon, global cache, B31/B33/B35 work or host adoption was added, matching the plan's exclusions.

Lock directories and the lock file are checked against symlink, non-regular and escape substitution, with SameFile confirmed after open (governance_write_guard.go:437-548). Foreign writes require explicit root bindings and the exact project set (governance_scoped_write.go:68-98). Outputs use root digests, not absolute paths. The executable digest checks the regular file, opened identity and bounded size (review_run_provenance.go:225-255). The live delegation policy is not shipped (distpolicy.go:118). No secrets were found.

The smallest sufficient alternative, re-hashing a few named files, would not bind directory listings, errors or federated roots, and would not prevent mixed producer results; the chosen design extends the existing Files seam with no daemon or cache. Cost: per-read mutex serialization and retained bytes up to the measured 512 MiB budget (no longer doubled after R1-F2). The choice would be invalidated if real corpora outgrew the D6 budgets without a new measurement, or if B35 runtime caching were adopted.
